newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS-Dollar/mark vols cool after leap with spot.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-Dollar/mark vols cool after leap with spot.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark deflated Wednesday morning after traders bid the one-month option as high as 11.1 percent in European trade, U.S. market participants said.

Dollar/mark vols began to climb late Tuesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's soothing Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the U.S. economy and monetary policy sent U.S. asset markets including the dollar soaring.

One-month volatility rose to 10.9/11.1 percent late Tuesday and extended the gain in Europe before settling back this morning to 10.4/10.6 percent, consistent with levels seen earlier in the previous day.

"Vols have come off because people are not sure we are going to continue to see such large gains in the spot," said John Bird, senior currency options analyst for Technical Data. "They see the move as a one-shot deal because of Greenspan."
The Greenspan effect carried the dollar to a new 71-month peak of 1.8325 against the mark in Europe.
In his remarks to Congress, Greenspan said the Fed may eventually have to change U.S. interest rates, but for now economic growth was moderating.

Dollar/mark risk reversals also narrowed slightly this morning, to 0.6/0.9 from 0.7/1.0 Tuesday for the one-month 25-delta options, still favoring mark puts but reflecting sentiment the pace of the dollar rally will slow, Bird said.
Buying of mark puts dominated activity overseas, where one bank was seen buying the one-month 1.8450 strike, two-month 1.8600 strike and one-year 1.9000 strike.
However, demand for the puts has quieted and volatility come off with the spot back below 1.83 marks, several U.S. traders said.
"It will be very spot-dependent," a Wall Street bank dealer said of volatility. "In general it has been a very disciplined move up, it's not whippy, so volatility should not go a lot higher."
Sterling/mark volatility also pulled back to 10.80/11.20 percent in the one-month option from opening levels of 11.25/11.60 percent following a new eight-year high in the spot.

The strong British economy and anticipation of higher U.K. interest rates continue to attract investors to the pound at the expense of the mark, whose eroding fortunes are tied to deepening sentiment that the euro will be a weak currency.
In dollar/yen, one-month volatility was steady at 10.1/10.3 percent, with risk reversals quoted at 0.5/0.75.
